To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the association of denatured nuclear DNA, mouse IgG, and C3 in GCW of NZB/NZW mice is a specific marker of lupus nephritis and that this complex may play a role in the pathogenesis.

NZB/NZW hybrids develop a lupus-like nephropathy in the 6th–7th month and that this disease is associated with the deposition of denatured deoxyribonucleoprotein and excess host immunoglobulin in the glomerular basement membrane.
the NZB/NZW mouse is a model of lupus nephritis and that the presence of nucleoside antigens in GCW of NZB/NZW hybrids is correlated with renal disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunologic aspects of a disease which has many similarities to human lupus erythematosus.
the study of the pathogenesis and immunopathology of lupus-like nephropathy in NZB/NZB F1 hybrid mice.
the study of the immunologic aspects of autoimmune disease in NZB/NZW F1 mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NZB/NZW hybrid mouse is a model of systemic lupus erythematosus.
the NZB mouse develops a disease which is very similar to the lupus erythematosus of humans.
in NZB/NZB F1 hybrids, the development of the nephritis is preceded by the appearance of an excess of mouse immunoglobulin in GCW and the formation of DNA-antibody complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NZB and NZB/NZW mice have a defect in the regulation of their antibody responses.
NZB/NZW mice, like NZB, have a defect in immunoregulation, but unlike NZB they also have the ability to produce a large quantity of IgG2b, the isotype most reactive in the nephritis.

(a) the NZB/NZW mouse is a good model for human systemic lupus erythematosus; (b) the NZB mouse is a model for the human disease with the exception of renal lesions; (c) the NZB/W F1 mouse is a model of human lupus nephritis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of DNA and IgG in the glomerulus is a good indicator of the development of autoimmune disease in mice.
we can use the mouse model of lupus to study the mechanisms of disease and to test new drugs.
the NZB/NZW hybrid mouse is an excellent model for studying human systemic lupus erythematosus, or SLE.
